unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 3: FEMA — Apply overseas-asset and repatriation provisions with their permissions, exceptions and defined meaning

facts.statement: Courseware defines repatriation, reproduces broad restrictions on dealing and holding overseas assets, and describes exporter declaration and repatriation duties. Its general no-overseas-holding statement is simplified.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 171–172; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Sections 4 and 8 are expressly qualified; section 6(4) permits specified foreign assets acquired while non-resident or inherited from a non-resident, and section 9 contains exemptions. Repatriation includes the specified sale to an authorised person, notified holding and use to discharge a foreign-currency debt. Section 7 addresses export declarations and section 8 reasonable steps within RBI-specified period/manner.

payload.title: Start with the restriction, then check its statutory qualifications
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 4 restricts resident holding and dealing in the specified foreign exchange, foreign securities and overseas immovable property **except as otherwise provided**. Those opening words matter. For example, Section 6(4) addresses specified assets acquired while the person was non-resident or inherited from a non-resident.

The correct bank workflow is to establish residence, acquisition history and the applicable permission or exception. Neither “all overseas assets are forbidden” nor “anything inherited is unrestricted for every purpose” is a sound substitute. The asset's later use and transaction-specific rules still need analysis.

self_check.prompt_text: Why should an overseas-asset file retain the history of acquisition and prior residence?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Those facts can be relevant to statutory qualifications such as Section 6(4), beyond the general holding restriction.

payload.title: Repatriation is a defined outcome with regulated methods
payload.core_explanation_md:
Repatriation is not simply a synonym for handing over foreign cash at a counter. Section 2(y) addresses bringing realised foreign exchange into India and the specified sale to an authorised person or notified account holding; it also includes use to discharge a foreign-currency debt or liability. Conditions and applicable permissions must still be checked.

Sections 7–8 separately address export declarations and reasonable steps to realise and repatriate amounts due or accrued, within the period and manner specified by RBI, subject to statutory qualifications. Do not infer one universal deadline from the bare Act or ignore an applicable exemption. The relevant dated RBI direction belongs with the transaction file.

self_check.prompt_text: Does the bare Act supply a single fixed realisation period for every export request?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. It refers to RBI-specified period and manner, with applicable qualifications and exemptions.

payload.stem_md: A returning resident holds a foreign asset acquired while non-resident. A branch cites only Section 4 and concludes that acquisition history is irrelevant. Which additional statutory provision should be examined?

options.text_md: Only the general restriction, without examining any statutory qualifications
options.explanation_md: The general restriction must be read with the Act provisions that permit the specified prior-acquired or inherited holdings.

options.text_md: Section 6(4), dealing with the specified prior-non-resident acquisition and inheritance cases
options.explanation_md: The asset history can engage a statutory qualification; the general restriction must not be read in isolation.

options.text_md: An unconditional permission arising from any historic overseas connection
options.explanation_md: The Act provides defined qualifications, not an unlimited exemption for every overseas connection.

options.text_md: An automatic exemption for every foreign asset held by an Indian citizen
options.explanation_md: Citizenship alone does not establish the residence and acquisition-history conditions of Section 6(4).

payload.correct_explanation_md: The asset history can engage a statutory qualification; the general restriction must not be read in isolation.

payload.stem_md: A team proposes one permanent export-realisation deadline based only on Section 8, without checking the applicable RBI direction. What is the main problem?

options.text_md: Section 8 never concerns foreign exchange due to residents
options.explanation_md: It expressly addresses foreign exchange due or accrued to persons resident in India.

options.text_md: All exporter declarations are optional in every case
options.explanation_md: The Act contains export declaration duties; the proposed blanket exemption is unsupported.

options.text_md: An exporter may choose any deadline by writing it on an invoice
options.explanation_md: A commercial invoice cannot replace the applicable legal period and conditions.

options.text_md: The section relies on RBI-specified period and manner, which need a dated source check
options.explanation_md: The bare Act alone does not establish one fixed operational period for every case.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The bare Act alone does not establish one fixed operational period for every case.

payload.stem_md: A training note defines repatriation exclusively as conversion of physical foreign notes to rupees and excludes every other route. Which correction follows Section 2(y)?

options.text_md: Remove every authorised-person condition from the definition
options.explanation_md: The statutory methods include authorised-person involvement and notified-account conditions.

options.text_md: Treat any private offshore account as sufficient in every case
options.explanation_md: The definition does not authorise unrestricted offshore retention.

options.text_md: Include the specified notified holding and foreign-currency liability discharge routes, subject to conditions
options.explanation_md: The definition is broader than physical-cash conversion, but its qualifications remain essential.

options.text_md: Apply only the customer's nationality to decide repatriation
options.explanation_md: Nationality alone does not define the permitted method of realisation and repatriation.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The definition is broader than physical-cash conversion, but its qualifications remain essential.
